validated_results.title: Protein intake and risk of renal cell cancer.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: Population-based case-control study reporting adjusted odds ratios for dietary protein intake quartiles and histologically confirmed incident renal cell cancer.

extraction.comparison_type: Fourth versus first quartile of protein intake

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 690 patients and 707 control subjects were interviewed.
sample_size.location: abstract; total_n derived from reported group counts 690 + 707 = 1397

cases.excerpt: Population-based control subjects were frequency-matched to cases by sex and 5-year age groups. A total of 690 patients and 707 control subjects were interviewed.

effect_size.excerpt: When examined by macronutrient status, risks increased monotonically with the amount of protein intake, from 1.2 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.7-1.9) to 1.4 (95% CI = 0.8-2.5) and 1.9 (95% CI = 1.0-3.6) (P for trend = .03) in the second, third, and fourth quartiles of intake, respectively, after adjustment for age, sex, caloric intake, body mass index, and cigarette smoking. No significant or consistent associations were detected with the intake of other dietary nutrients or beverages.

confidence_interval.excerpt: When examined by macronutrient status, risks increased monotonically with the amount of protein intake, from 1.2 (95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.7-1.9) to 1.4 (95% CI = 0.8-2.5) and 1.9 (95% CI = 1.0-3.6) (P for trend = .03) in the second, third, and fourth quartiles of intake, respectively, after adjustment for age, sex, caloric intake, body mass index, and cigarette smoking.

comparison.excerpt: in the second, third, and fourth quartiles of intake, respectively, after adjustment for age, sex, caloric intake, body mass index, and cigarette smoking

design.excerpt: Control subjects were selected from the general population of Minnesota residents

timing.excerpt: renal cell cancer that had been diagnosed between July 1, 1988, and December 31, 1990

continent.excerpt: white residents of Minnesota between 20 and 79 years of age

ethnicity.excerpt: The patients eligible for inclusion in this study were white residents of Minnesota

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Usual adult dietary intakes were assessed by questionnaire

gender.excerpt: Patients and control subjects were similar in distribution by sex, age, and educational level.
